p: If the volcano theme gets the kids curious, Edinburgh is the perfect city to explore it further. Dynamic Earth, near Holyrood, is an interactive science centre that takes you through the story of our planet, from its fiery beginnings to ice ages and rainforests. It's a natural follow-up to a round of jungle golf, and it's under cover too. Arthur's Seat itself is part of an ancient volcano, so you can tell the kids they're walking on one if you head up there.
Prefer gardens? The Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh, a short way north of the centre, is a beautiful place for a wander, with sweeping lawns, a rock garden and big views back towards the castle.

For the golf itself, it's all about reading each hole. Look for the slopes and angles before you putt, and use the walls to your advantage. A smooth, gentle stroke usually gets the ball closer than a big smack. Agree on a shot limit per hole before you start, especially with younger players, to keep things moving and stop anyone getting frustrated.
Whether you're a tourist after a break from castles and closes or a local looking for an easy indoor plan, a round here is a cheery way to fill an hour. Let the winner choose the next stop.
